lines.text: There are different groups of migrants [migranten]: you have a Dutch partner (marriage migrant [huwelijksmigrant]) or Dutch family (family migrant [familiemigrant]); you come as a refugee [vluchteling]; you want to work (labour migrant [arbeidsmigrant], or expat); or you want to study.
Do you want to stay in the Netherlands longer than ninety days and do you come from outside the European Union [Europese Unie (EU)]?
Then you need a residence permit [verblijfsvergunning].
Two groups must also complete civic integration [inburgeren]:

Marriage and family migrants [Huwelijksmigranten en familiemigranten]: before you may come to the Netherlands, you must take the basic civic integration exam [basisexamen inburgering], at about A1 level, usually in your own country at the embassy [ambassade].
You usually first need authorization for temporary stay [mvv, machtiging tot voorlopig verblijf] — that is a visa.
In the Netherlands you must complete civic integration within three years, usually at language level B1.
Refugees [Vluchtelingen]: you must apply for asylum [asiel].
You are an asylum seeker [asielzoeker] until you have a positive answer.
Then you become a status holder [statushouder] and must also complete civic integration within three years, usually at B1.
A residence permit is at first for a fixed period [bepaalde tijd] — temporary [tijdelijk], with an end date [einddatum].
You must extend [verlengen] your permit before that date passes.
Have you been legally in the Netherlands for five years or longer?
Then you can apply for a residence permit for an indefinite period [onbepaalde tijd] — without an end date.
There are conditions [voorwaarden]: your income must be high enough and you must have finished your civic integration.
Naturalization [Naturalisatie] means that you receive Dutch nationality [Nederlandse nationaliteit].
This is possible if you have been legally in the Netherlands for five years or longer, or three years with a Dutch partner, and have finished your civic integration.
With a Dutch passport you have more rights and you can travel to other countries.
You can also apply for the nationality for your children.
Usually you can not keep your old nationality; in some situations dual nationality is allowed, for example if you are Moroccan — you must always keep the Moroccan nationality.
The Immigration and Naturalisation Service [IND, Immigratie- en Naturalisatiedienst] decides on residence permits.
Applying, extending and collecting are done at the IND.
A passport, identity card and Dutch nationality are applied for at the municipality [gemeente].
Each document costs money.
